root_cause.text: The use of a shared bitfield word for `claimed` and retune control flags (`can_retune`, `retune_now`, `retune_paused`) introduced non-atomic read-modify-write races where concurrent updates from different contexts could corrupt each other's bits, leading to spurious assertion failures.
root_cause.evidence: Commit message states: "Writes to claimed in __mmc_claim_host() or retune_now in mmc_mq_queue_rq() can overwrite other bits when concurrent updates happen in other contexts, triggering spurious WARN_ON(!host->claimed)." Patch moves `claimed`, `can_retune`, `retune_now`, and `retune_paused` from bitfields to separate `bool` fields to eliminate shared-word coupling.

vuln_statements.content: unsigned int		claimed:1;	/* host exclusively claimed */
unsigned int		can_retune:1;	/* re-tuning can be used */
unsigned int		retune_now:1;	/* do re-tuning at next req */
unsigned int		retune_paused:1;	/* re-tuning is temporarily disabled */

intent_record.intent_summary: Add boolean fields to struct mmc_host for clearer re-tuning state management, preparing for improved re-tuning control logic.
intent_record.what: Added three boolean fields (can_retune, retune_now, retune_paused) to the struct mmc_host definition, positioned before the existing need_retune, hold_retune, and retune_period fields.
intent_record.how: The struct now includes explicit boolean flags to control re-tuning: can_retune indicates if re-tuning is supported, retune_now forces re-tuning at the next request, and retune_paused temporarily disables re-tuning.
